newsitem.title: USA: USTR's Barshefsky announces new program on Africa.
newsitem.headline: USTR's Barshefsky announces new program on Africa.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Tuesday that the Clinton administration has a new "economic approach" to Africa which emphasizes support for countries making strong efforts on trade liberalization.
The program is called "Partnership for Promoting Economic Growth and Opportunity in Africa," Barshefsky said in testimony for a congressional hearing.

"The most dramatic progress has come when countries have focused on three areas: trade and investment liberalization, investing in human resources, and improving policy management. Our program seeks to emphasize suppport for countries that are making strong efforts in these areas," she said.

Barshefsky also said that any Sub-Saharan country that is not already a member of the World Trade Organizaiton "should be actively pursuing membership in the WTO and be prepared to take on meaningful obligations."

Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers told the subcommittee that the United States would support efforts to reduce the debt burden of African countries that move to liberalize trade and investment.

Summers said the United States would support an approach that leads to elimination of concessional bilateral debt for the poorest countries that undertake bold reforms. Washington, he said, would urge the World Bank and International Monetary Fund to provide maximum relief under the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC) debt initiative for eligible countries.

"The budgets of many African countries are both heavily burdened by debt service and highly dependent on revenues from trade taxes," Summers said in prepared testimony. "Typically 40 to 50 percent of total budget revenues come from trade taxes.
"We want to see to it that aggressively liberalizing countries have enough breathing space to carry through with a comprehensive program of trade liberalization and tax reforms," Summers said.
